observations: First-generation PlayStation 4 ('Fat') console, identifiable by its two-tier angular design.
The console is covered in a grey, white, and black camouflage vinyl wrap.
A black Sony DualSense controller (native to PS5) is shown on top of the console.
Watermark 'STEVAN ZIDIRI' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' is visible on all three photos.
No images show the console's rear ports, serial number plate, or the system software in operation.

claims.evidence: Requires a photo of the system settings or home screen showing custom firmware (e.g., GoldHEN).
No photos of the digital library or physical game discs are provided. Note: FC 27 is consistent with the 2026 market date.
The vinyl skin covers the entire exterior, preventing assessment of the original surface condition.
The factory warranty seals on the rear of the console are not shown.
The controller shown is a PS5 DualSense, which is not the original controller for a PS4 console. Also, 'pads' implies multiple, but only one is pictured.
The receipt is mentioned but not pictured.

risks.risk: The console may be on a firmware version that cannot be hacked.
risks.proof: A photo of Settings > System > System Information.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a standard unhacked console.

risks.risk: The PS5 controller may not be compatible or may be a low-quality clone.
risks.proof: A video of the controller being used to play a game on this specific console.
risks.if_unproven: priced as if no controller is included.

risks.risk: The vinyl skin may be hiding significant cosmetic damage or cracks.
risks.proof: Photos of the console with the skin removed.

risks.risk: The internal storage capacity is unconfirmed.
risks.proof: A photo of the Storage menu in system settings.

proof_requests: Photo of the System Information screen showing the firmware version.
Photo of the Storage screen showing the hard drive capacity.
Photo of the back of the console showing the ports and warranty seals.
Video of the console booting up and launching a game using the provided controller.
response.reason: The console is identifiable as a PS4 Fat. While the hacking and games are unproven, and the controller is from a different generation, it can be valued at the worst-case price for a basic PS4 Fat unit.
